transcript: Eureka Day by Jonathan Spector is a great example of a play that's topical and thought-provoking but still dramatically motivated. Currently running on Broadway at the Friedman, this is a one-act comedy about a private elementary school's executive board. They pride themselves on being super inclusive but are forced to rethink their vaccination policy when there's a mumps outbreak at the school. Knowing this premise, I honestly worried this would be a cringey attempt at making a caricature of a well-meaning but out of touch group of people — a concept I feel has been beaten to death recently. But it ended up being, I thought, a genuinely funny, fascinating, and intelligent meditation on community, cooperation, and hubris, while handling difficult topics with empathy and reason. I thought the pacing was outstanding, the 90 minutes or so absolutely flew by, and the cast was small but mighty with standouts including Jessica Hecht and Amber Gray. Manhattan Theater Club has had quite a streak of great work at the Friedman recently and Eureka Day continues it. With that, another playbill for my collection.
